issue: Review PR adding new API endpoints

observations.summary: Added input size limits to prevent DoS via unbounded payloads
observations.detail: All user-supplied fields now have maximum size limits: productId (255 chars), items array (100 per order), quantity (999,999), unitPrice (999,999.99), and cursor query parameter (1,000 chars). Without these limits, an attacker could send megabyte-sized productId strings, arrays with 100k+ items, or extremely long cursor values to exhaust server memory and CPU. Limits are enforced in isValidOrderItem() and isValidItemsArray() validation functions and as a pre-validation check for cursor in listOrders().

observations.summary: Extracted validation limit constants for maintainability
observations.detail: Replaced magic numbers in validation with named constants (MAX_PRODUCT_ID_LENGTH, MAX_ITEMS_PER_ORDER, MAX_QUANTITY, MAX_UNIT_PRICE, MAX_CURSOR_LENGTH). These constants are defined at module scope in orders.ts and referenced in both validation logic and error messages, ensuring consistency and making future limit adjustments a single-line change.

observations.summary: Fixed error table: removed nonexistent 403 FORBIDDEN, added validation limits
observations.detail: The API docs listed a FORBIDDEN (403) error code that never occurs in the implementation — IDOR protection returns 404 instead. Removed the 403 entry and clarified that NOT_FOUND (404) is also returned for non-owner access. Added a new Validation Limits table documenting all field constraints (items array size, productId length, quantity/unitPrice ranges, cursor/limit bounds).

observations.summary: Added 8 new boundary validation tests bringing total to 62
observations.detail: Added tests for: (1) productId exceeding 255 chars rejected, (2) productId at 255 chars accepted, (3) items array >100 rejected, (4) items array at 100 accepted, (5) quantity >999999 rejected, (6) unitPrice >999999.99 rejected, (7) cursor >1000 chars rejected, (8) whitespace-only productId behavior documented. All 62 tests passing.

observations.summary: All user-supplied string/array inputs should have explicit size limits
observations.detail: Any API endpoint accepting user input should enforce maximum sizes for strings (productId, cursor, etc.) and arrays (items) to prevent denial-of-service attacks. This convention is now implemented in the order endpoints and should be followed for any future endpoints (e.g., /api/invoices, /api/products). Validation limits should be defined as named constants and documented in the API reference.
